question.problem:
What is the remainder of $-4{x}^{4}-{x}^{2}-9$ divided by ${x}^{2}-2x+3?$

The remainder is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the ${x}^{3}$ and $x$ terms. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing terms with zero coefficients, as follows:

$$
-4{x}^{4}-{x}^{2}-9=-4{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+0x-9
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,-4{x}^{2}-8x-5 \\  & {x}^{2}-2x+3\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,-4{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}-\phantom{00}{x}^{2}+\phantom{0}0x-\phantom{0}9\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{\,-4{x}^{4}+8{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,-8{x}^{3}+11{x}^{2}+0x-9 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{-\,8{x}^{3}+16{x}^{2}-24x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,-5{x}^{2}+24x-9 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{-5{x}^{2}+10x-15}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,14x+6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

- the quotient is $-4{x}^{2}-8x-5,$ and

- the remainder is $14x+6.$
